solarize columbia campaign nears completion solarize columbia nears completion as advocates push renewables cite strong enrollment and urge public input on the citys longterm energy plan the initiative launched july 2025 by national energy provider solarcrowdsource offered free noobligation solar evaluations and up to 20 group discounts nearly 160 columbia property owners enrolled before the september deadline the program involves a tiered pricing system the more people that participate the less money everyone pays the coalition said in a news release carolyn amparan chair of the midmissouri chapter of the sierra club said expanding renewable energy is a matter of public importance we need people who care about renewable energy to contact state officials amparan said we all need to care about the impacts of climate change as part of its final phase the campaign is encouraging residents to provide input to city leaders as they develop the integrated resource plan which will guide energy decisions for the next 20 years this effort builds on the campaigns initial focus of securing residential solar contracts through solarcrowdsource mark haim director of midmissouri peaceworks said columbia must accelerate its transition from coal to solar and wind power to reduce its carbon footprint midmissouri peaceworks has advocated for renewable energy for decades there is an urgent need to address the climate crisis and the best thing we can do here in columbia is switch our source of electricity from predominantly coal to both renewable solar and wind haim said columbias baseload electric needs are currently met by three coalfired power plants the sikeston power plant the iatan generating station and the prairie state energy campus there are costs not incorporated into the price of electricity when we dont move away from caustic sources like coal haim said adding that failing to invest in renewable energy carries significant consequences for people and the planet haim said investments in renewable energy and efficiency improvements are worth the cost and urged leaders and residents to consider future generations the campaign follows the collapse of the city of columbias boone stephens solar project eight months ago the project failed due to economic factors prompting the proposed contractor enel north america to withdraw according to previous missourian reporting as a result the city did not meet its 2024 renewable energy goal but is said to be on track to reach 30 renewable energy by dec 31 2028 jon dolan executive director for the missouri solar energy industries association complimented the city on the way residents embrace rooftop solar panels he described columbia as one of the most progressive and smart cities in renewables the city has about 130000 residents including a large student population with energy usage shaped by residential demand and health care facilities the deadline to sign residential contracts was saturday but commercial contracts can be signed until april 30 installations are expected to be completed by dec 31 more information about the campaign can be found at the solarize columbia website

the moon a silent regulator of earth not a symbol the moon is often treated as a metaphor for loneliness or mystery but in reality it plays a precise and measurable role in earths stability its gravitational pull controls ocean tides which directly affect marine ecosystems coastal climates and even nutrient circulation in the oceans the moon also stabilizes earths axial tilt reducing extreme climate shifts over long periods without it earths climate would be far more chaotic the moon doesnt emit its own light doesnt influence life emotionally and isnt watching us it reflects sunlight and follows predictable orbital mechanics governed by gravity and angular momentum its phases are not transformationsjust changes in how much of its sunlit surface is visible from earth calling the moon lonely or mysterious is human projection scientifically it is a natural satellite formed likely from debris after a massive impact early in earths history now locked in a stable orbit its not symbolic its functional and earth depends on it more than we casually realize

elegant voice of a movement the kuow book club read positive obsession the life and times of octavia e butler by susana m morris this month im your reading guide katie campbell morris joined me on zoom recently to talk about her biography of a literary legend listen to our full conversation by hitting the play button above by katie campbell 20251229 the kuow book club is reading positive obsession the life and times of octavia e butler by susana m morris in december 2025 design by katie campbell the moment susana m morris first came upon a novel by octavia butler could have been the setup for one of the great science fiction authors stories morris was 15 wandering through her public librarys science fiction section this was fort lauderdale fla in the mid90s her options were limited this was also the era of shows like candid camera and punkd so when she saw a copy of parable of the sower with the cover facing out as if it was there just for her morris thought she was being pranked when i saw the book and saw that it had been written by a black woman and there was a black woman on the cover i thought this is not real yall are setting me up wheres the camera morris told me morris suddenly saw herself reflected in a genre dominated by white men and white male characters shed found one of butlers most celebrated novels one that centered a young black woman like morris some librarian said im going to not just file this here but im going to face the cover out so that someone can see it those are choices that librarians make morris said maybe it was an afterthought or maybe it was a very intentional kind of situation but i thank them regardless because it really changed the trajectory of my life since then morris has become an educator a scholar of afrofuturism and an author herself and in her latest work positive obsession the life and times of octavia e butler she paid homage to the woman who sent her down that path it was not easy being an architect an astronaut an engineer and an innovator octavia did not grow up in the world we have now flawed though it may be but she did help positively shape the world that we are now inheriting by centering black women as heroines not as sidekicks or vehicles for others growth by crafting cautionary tales that charge us all with creating the future we want to see and by being an example of what persistence matched with brilliance can do octavias writing implores us that it is up to us to reimagine the world we want to live in and do the work to create it and in that way octavias genius changed the worldpositive obsession page 213 butler was key to the development of afrofuturism which morris described as a movement that frames african diasporic cultural practices as central to the continuation of human society butlers stories centered black women in particular and asked difficult questions about humanitys hierarchal tendencies though she wrote fiction butler also tried to warn readers about threats she saw on the horizon climate change the rise of white nationalism and fascism the breakdown of social safety nets when the kuow book club read fledgling the last novel butler published before she died suddenly in her lake forest park home i spoke to her longtime friend and fellow author nisi shawl i was surprised when shawl said this of butler i honestly dont know if she would have been able to keep writing because she was already doing her utmost to put an optimistic spin on what she wrote 40 years ago related fledgling is octavia butlers unfinished but fundamental legacy book club checkin i asked morris what she thought of that i can see that being the case she may have been so frustrated because she wasnt the only person warning us morris said she was probably the most eloquent and elegant voice saying it but she was part of a chorus she was leading a chorus of folks saying these are things we need to pay attention to there are ways in which our society is not working if you like me are sad to think of a universe in which butler no longer felt like her writing her positive obsession was worth it anymore be heartened by this from morris epilogue luckily for us octavias works are not simply doomsday tales bent on scaring us into submission positive obsession page 2215 submission after all would be antithetical to butlers entire life her legacy morris went on octavias hope that we would read her work and then be incited to study our world and our misshaping of it and be spurred into action is a noble hope noble and necessary though her works often depict a future marred by violence and injustice these stories were not nihilistic predictions but a sort of love offering for readers to receive and be changed by and to that end what a gift they are octavias messages presuppose that we are smart enough and justiceoriented enough to be introspective and to make life better for generations to come this is the ultimate gesture of hope for humanity positive obsession page 218 morris biography of butler is a continuation of that gesture of hope positive obsession is both a lovingly detailed account of butlers life and a sort of refresher course on her work the research that went into it and the lasting legacy she left butlers strength of imagination and will paved the way for literary greats like rivers solomon and n k jemisin the world was robbed when butler died at just 58 years old but the literary landscape she sowed continues to thrive morris work both as an author and an educator who teaches butlers work is a testament to that lets not forget too the small role the pacific northwest played in butlers story albeit later in her life moving to seattle gave octavia an opportunity to live in an area that she found breathtaking where she could explore state parks hike and commune with nature there was also a vibrant science fiction community in the pacific northwest she still kept copious journals and filled them with musings about politics pop culture her natural surroundings and of course her writing but gone were the days when she filled pages of her diary with yearnings for a different kind of life these days octavia was mostly settled if not at peace with the direction her personal life had taken she was not incessantly mourning that she was missing out on something now in her fifties hers was a quiet life centered on her work and dotted with conversations with a wide range of acquaintances colleagues students mentees fans and family activities with her small tightknit circle of friends and restorative sojourns into the beautiful terrain of the pacific northwest positive obsession page 183 in answer to the classic if you could have dinner with anyone dead or alive question i often choose butler but after reading this passage i would have preferred to join her on one of those sojourns i like to think of her wandering the olympic peninsula at ease and in love with her surroundings i wonder too how she might have felt to see the place where she made her home become unaffordable to so many to see how the tech sector changed seattle and how the covid pandemic would permanently change the world though nisi shawl and morris certainly know her better i like to think butler would have kept writing into old age perhaps she would have written the fledgling sequel or continued the parable series or perhaps she would have written something entirely new something poignant about book bans or lgbtq rights or ai can you imagine i think she couldve related new biography shows how octavia butler deserved better early in her career

scalp care vancouver essential tips for healthy strong hair when it comes to hair health most of us focus solely on shampoos conditioners and styling products but the real secret to luscious locks starts at the rootquite literally scalp tattooing health is the foundation of strong beautiful hair and for residents of vancouver where the climate can be both damp and drying its even more important to give your scalp the attention it deserves why scalp care matters your scalp is an extension of your skin yet its often overlooked in daily selfcare routines a healthy scalp promotes better hair growth prevents dandruff and reduces irritation or itching neglecting your scalp can lead to clogged follicles dryness and even hair thinning over time hair restoration vancouver in vancouver where weather patterns fluctuate between rainy winters and sunny summers the scalp faces unique challenges the humidity can lead to excess oil production while cooler windy days might strip your scalp of natural moisture this combination calls for a specialized scalp care routine tailored to vancouvers climate scalp care tips for vancouver residents 1 hydrate and moisturize vancouvers colder months can leave your scalp feeling dry and itchy incorporate a hydrating scalp serum or mask into your routine to lock in moisture look for ingredients like hyaluronic acid aloe vera and natural oils to nourish your scalp 2 exfoliate regularly exfoliation isnt just for your face removing dead skin cells and buildup from your scalp is crucial for maintaining healthy follicles use a gentle scalp scrub once a week to keep your scalp fresh and free of debris 3 choose the right shampoo select shampoos that cater to your specific scalp needs if youre dealing with dryness opt for sulfatefree formulas enriched with natural oils for oily scalps a clarifying shampoo can help regulate excess sebum production 4 protect against weather changes vancouvers unpredictable weather means your scalp needs extra protection wear a hat during colder months to shield your scalp from harsh winds and uv rays and dont forget to use a uvprotectant spray during sunny summer days 5 seek professional scalp treatments for those dealing with persistent scalp issues consider visiting a trichologist or scalp specialist vancouver is home to a growing number of hair clinics and salons that offer targeted scalp treatments to address conditions like dandruff psoriasis and thinning hair popular scalp care treatments in vancouver vancouvers beauty and wellness scene is teeming with options for scalp care from highend salons offering detoxifying scalp facials to holistic clinics providing infrared light therapy theres something for everyone many local salons also use ecofriendly vegan products to available right here in vancouver and experience the transformation from the root up

beyond tribes and flags why the future of artificial intelligence must help humanity outgrow the myth of the nation for most of its history humanity lived without nations huntergatherer bands formed dissolved and recombined agricultural villages rose and fell empires expanded and fragmented yet the modern idea of the nationstatea bounded population united by shared ancestry culture and destinyemerged only within the last few centuries it is a recent invention born not from biology but from political necessity today this invention is increasingly strained migration flows global communication and economic interdependence have blurred the boundaries that once seemed stable genes mix faster than flags can define them languages merge and mutate cultures interpenetrate the concept of a permanent homogeneous people begins to look less like a scientific category and more like a convenient fiction from the perspective of biology animal behavior and artificial intelligence this fiction carries danger it transforms flexible social identities into rigid biological myths it recasts dynamic human populations as eternal tribes and it encourages conflict by framing political competition as existential struggle between imagined essences if artificial intelligence is to play a constructive role in humanitys future it must not merely optimize productivity or automate labor it must help human societies abandon outdated identity frameworks and move toward forms of coordination grounded in shared vulnerability rather than mutual fear there are no biological nations in biological terms a species can be defined a subspecies can sometimes be justified but a nation cannot human genetic variation is continuous rather than clustered traits change gradually across geography not in sharp borders two individuals from opposite ends of a continent may differ less genetically than two individuals from neighboring villages what people call ethnic groups are usually the result of recent historical bottlenecks cultural boundaries or political labelingnot deep evolutionary separation from an evolutionary perspective humanity is young and mobile modern homo sapiens spread across the globe in less than 70000 years that is not enough time to form biologically distinct populations comparable to subspecies in other animals what exists instead is a mosaic overlapping gradients of ancestry shaped by migration trade conquest and intermarriage yet nationstates present these gradients as partitions they convert probability clouds into borders they tell stories of ancient bloodlines and permanent homelands even when historical and genetic evidence shows constant mixing this transformation is not accidental it is administrative to govern large populations states require legibility taxes must be collected soldiers recruited laws enforced it is easier to rule a population that can be named categorized and symbolically unified the people becomes a managerial abstraction the nation becomes a moral object over time this abstraction is naturalized what began as a political tool is reinterpreted as biological destiny tribal psychology without tribes animal behavior reveals why this process is so powerful many social species rely on ingroup recognition wolves distinguish pack members primates track alliances birds defend territories these mechanisms evolved to manage smallscale cooperation and competition they operate on direct perception and repeated interaction human brains still carry these mechanisms we are exquisitely sensitive to group membership we infer loyalty from accents clothing and rituals we feel safety among us and threat from them but modern nations are too large to be directly perceived no human can personally know millions of compatriots the nation therefore exists only symbolicallythrough flags myths and narratives yet the emotional circuits that evolved for villagesized groups are hijacked by abstract identities this mismatch produces instability a cognitive system evolved to manage dozens of relationships is asked to emotionally represent millions of strangers the result is overgeneralization strangers are imagined as kin and other strangers as enemies from an ethological perspective this is a category error humans evolved to manage coalitions dynamically not to embody static essences real groups in nature form and dissolve based on context food availability mating opportunities threats identity is situational nationalism freezes this fluidity it asserts that group membership is permanent inherited and morally binding it treats history as destiny the nation as a story machine sociology shows how this freezing occurs nations are not simply populations they are narratives they require founding myths shared heroes and common trauma they depend on selective memory and strategic forgetting complex histories of migration and mixture are simplified into linear genealogies this narrative compression resembles language itself a manydimensional reality reduced to a single storyline it enables coordination but at the cost of distortion the danger arises when stories of belonging become stories of exclusion when difference is framed as threat when competition is framed as survival from a systems perspective nationalism transforms political disagreement into existential conflict economic disputes become civilizational struggles policy failures become betrayals of identity the flexibility of negotiation is replaced by the rigidity of myth in such systems violence becomes easier to justify if the group is eternal and sacred then its enemies must be permanent and profane history shows the consequences the twentieth centurys largest catastrophes were not driven by resource scarcity alone but by ideologies of ethnic destiny and national purity these ideologies treated human variation as contamination rather than continuity why this matters for artificial intelligence artificial intelligence now enters this social landscape like language ai is a compression system it reduces vast complexity into simplified representations it categorizes predicts and labels it constructs models of human behavior from historical data this creates a profound risk ai may inherit the same fictional categories that human societies invented for political convenience it may learn nations and ethnicities as if they were natural kinds rather than administrative constructs it may optimize decisions around group labels that have no biological coherence transient coalitions within a single interbreeding species dynamic populations not eternal peoples from a biological and behavioral perspective human populations should be modeled as dynamic flows informed ai would instead model populations as overlapping probability distributions it would track behavior patterns rather than inherited labels it would treat culture as mutable and identity as contextdependent such an approach aligns more closely with evolutionary theory and with the empirical record of human history the future of social coordination the deeper question is not technical but philosophical what kind of social coordination should intelligent systems support nationstates solved a real problem in their time how to organize large populations for defense taxation and law but they did so by converting administrative units into emotional identities they turned governance into belonging this solution now produces diminishing returns in a globally interconnected world challenges such as climate change pandemics and technological risk do not respect borders yet national frameworks incentivize zerosum competition rather than shared response future human identity is single adaptive system with internal diversity it could emphasize interdependence rather than separation it could optimize cooperation without erasing difference from identity to interaction one way to frame this shift is to move from identitybased models to interactionbased models instead of asking which group does this person belong to intelligent systems could ask how does this person behave biology organisms do not classify each other by origin they respond to signals threat is inferred from behavior not from lineage cooperation emerges from repeated interaction not from shared myths such a framework would treat human society as an ecosystem rather than a mosaic of fortresses the myth that must expire the nationstate is not evil it is obsolete it solved a historical coordination danger is not that humans will have identities it is that they will define those identities through exclusion and fear ai will not decide this for us but it will encode whichever worldview we give it if we train it on tribal myths it will become a more efficient tribalist if we train it on dynamic models of humanity it may become a stabilizer rather than an amplifier conclusion intelligence without enemies from the standpoint of biology there is only one human species from the standpoint of animal behavior there are only shifting coalitions from the standpoint of sociology there are only stories we choose to tell about ourselves artificial intelligence now joins this story as a new participant in social modeling it will not merely predict human behavior it will help shape it the question is whether it will inherit the logic of the pastnations as natural kinds conflict as destinyor help humanity move toward a different frame populations as fluid cooperation as adaptive and identity as plural rather than singular future societies will still differ they will still argue they will still compete but their identities need not be built on mutual dehumanization a truly advanced intelligence would not divide humanity into eternal tribes it would recognize humanity as a single evolving system with many temporary patterns nations were a story we once needed they should not become the story that destroys us if artificial intelligence is to be more than a mirror of human fear it must help us see ourselves not as rival peoples but as one species learning imperfectly how to live together on a changing planet

three worlds were created and destroyedwe live in the fourth world in the myths and sacred texts of various peoples worldwide a recurring motif exists about the sequential destruction and renewal of the world often it specifically concerns three preceding ages or worlds that perished due to global catastrophes while humanity lives in the fourth these narratives despite the geographical and cultural distance of their sources show a striking similarity in describing events reminiscent of largescale geophysical changes such as shifts in the earths axis floods and the fall of celestial bodies biblical and classical evidence biblical texts contain descriptions that can be interpreted as evidence of global upheavals the book of isaiah states the earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard and it shall fall and not rise again the gospel of matthew describes signs preceding the end times the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light the stars will fall from heaven and the powers of the heavens will be shaken similar motifs are present in the psalms where the earth trembles and the heavens fall at the presence of the deity in classical tradition ovid in metamorphoses describes a catastrophe related to phaeton when the sunchariot went off course and constellations tried to plunge into the ocean plato in timaeus discusses the earth moving in all six directions mythology of the golden age and the change of the world axis the concept of the worlds initial ideal state often called the golden age is linked to a different celestial arrangement greek philosophers anaxagoras and anaximenes believed that initially the stars revolved in a horizontal plane and the pole star was at the zenith this suggests an idea of the absence of the earths axial tilt which theoretically should have created eternal spring on the planet similar ideas are found in other cultures japanese chinese egyptian the egyptian magical papyrus harris speaks of a cataclysm when the south becomes north and the earth is overturned cycles of destruction in hopi and other traditions the concept of sequentially destroyed worlds is most fully represented in the mythology of the hopi people according to their traditions four worlds were created the first world tokpela was destroyed by fire the second world tokpa by glaciation the third world kuskurza by a great flood the current fourth world tuwaqachi continues to exist but its fate depends on human behavior a key element in the story of the second worlds destruction is the departure from their posts of the twin poles guarding the world axis this led to a loss of balance the world spun crazily then turned over twice after which it was covered in ice similar memories are preserved among other indigenous peoples of the americas the pawnee indians spoke of a time when the pole stars changed places greenland eskimos remember an era when the earth capsized in the scandinavian edda the end of the world ragnark is described through the release of the wolf fenrir which causes the shaking of the world tree yggdrasil a symbol of the world axis the destruction of mountains and the fall of stars ancient chinese chronicles and interpretation of catastrophes ancient chinese sources also contain detailed descriptions of chaos that ensued after humanitys rebellion against heaven the planets altered their courses the sky sank lower to the north the sun moon and stars changed their motion the earth fell apart into pieces furthermore legends of many peoples feature periods of unnaturally prolonged darkness or conversely continuous day one possible interpretation of these stories suggests they could be allegorical descriptions of the consequences of a sudden change in the earths axial tilt if the axis assumed a position close to horizontal at an angle of about 90 degrees extremely long polar nights and days would occur over much of the planet which could be described as eternal darkness or the sun not setting below the horizon thus a crosscultural analysis of mythology demonstrates the existence of a universal narrative about the cyclical history of humanity linked to global geophysical upheavals these traditions viewed not as a literal chronicle but as memory of real catastrophic events from deep antiquity encoded in symbols continue to raise questions about our planets stability and its climatic history they represent a unique layer of collective human experience offering an alternative mythopoetic perspective on the origin and fate of the world

world building advice non fantasy elements worldbuilding advice for nonfantasy elements 1 research and realism ground your world in thorough research and realism understand the historical cultural and geographical aspects relevant to your setting to create an authentic and believable environment 2 consider societal structures explore the societal structures and institutions that shape your world consider the political economic and social systems and examine how they influence the characters and plot 3 setting as a character treat the setting as a character in itself how does the environment impact the mood tone and dynamics of the story whether urban or rural the setting should contribute to the narrative in meaningful ways 4 timeline and history develop a timeline and history for your world considering significant events that have shaped the current state of affairs historical context adds depth to the narrative and informs character motivations 5 diverse characters and perspectives populate your world with diverse characters each with their own backgrounds experiences and perspectives this not only reflects reality but also enriches the narrative by offering varied viewpoints 6 technology and progress consider the level of technological advancement in your world how does technology impact daily life communication and societal structures technological elements can shape the narrative and add layers to your world 7 cultural nuances explore the cultural nuances within your world what languages do people speak what customs and traditions define their societies pay attention to details that showcase the richness of cultural diversity 8 economic realities delve into the economic aspects of your world how do people earn a living what industries drive the economy economic conditions can be a significant factor influencing character motivations and conflicts 9 climate and geography consider the climate and geography of your world these elements impact agriculture travel and the overall lifestyle of the inhabitants natural features also contribute to the atmosphere of the story 10 show everyday life provide glimpses into the everyday lives of your characters what do they eat wear and do for recreation these details add texture to your world and make it more relatable to readers 11 evolution of society explore how societies in your world have evolved over time consider societal shifts advancements and cultural changes that have shaped the present state of affairs this historical context provides depth to your worldbuilding remember that even in a nonfantasy setting the world should serve as a dynamic and integral aspect of your narrative influencing and being influenced by the characters and events in your story

coolant not only lowers the freezing point but also has two more very important jobs 1 coolant lubricates your water pump 2 coolant protects your engine and radiator from inner corrosion volvo recommends for the p80 p2 platform g11g48 coolant these coolants use silicates to protect your aluminium engine blocks by forming a silicatecover but those silicates are used up after 23 years after p80 and p2 platforms regarding the p1 and p3 platform i cannot reliably assure that my guide is applicable regarding the spa platform these cars have very complex cooling systems this guide is not suited for those cars the method i am describing is cheap and really easy to do yourself no car lift not even ramps are required just some basic utensils and a socket wrench the only downside of this method is that it is quite timeconsuming youll need 5 liter 5 quarts of coolant concentrate further down below i discuss which kind is the best 2550 liters of distilled water if you have really soft tap water that could be an alternative but i wouldnt recommend it a socket wrench set a funnel a rather flat 1015 liter catch pan that fits under your car a big measuring cup 5 liter 5 quarts not necessary but helpful paper towels which coolant should i use volvo recommends g11 zerex g48 coolant for the p80 and p2 platform but as mentioned in the beginning this type of coolant needs to be g11 g48 it could go lumpy and could block the coolant flow lets get started 1 remove the splash guard it is typically held on by 2 screws these 2 screws are on the left and right side arms of the splash guard it is sometimes also clipped in by two clips those will unclip if you press on them 2 locate the lower radiator hose dont bother opening the drain plug these are mostly made of plastic and will due to their age and exposure to heat break off easily if that happens you will likely need an expert and in the worst case a new radiator 3 locate the hose clamp which clamps the lower radiator hose to the radiator open up this hose clamp 4 place your pan underneath the lower radiator hose and pull it off the radiator this is a bit messy but try to catch all coolant coming out animals love coolant because it tastes sweet but it is fatal if swallowed now take off your coolant tank cap 5 refit the lower radiator hose and tighten the hose clamp dont overtighten 6 measure how out there is a second drain plug at the back of the engine but i strongly advise you not to use it because a you need ramps or a lift and b it is a brass fitting which is most likely corroded and will break off when you try to loosen it if it breaks off you have a big problem not worth it 7 use the funnel to fill the system with distilled water fill it up really slowly it is normal that you at that your heater core is getting flushed as well 10 leave the engine idle for 35 min your coolant level will most likely drop immediately after starting the engine so just top up to the max line again 11 screw on your coolant tank cap and take your car for a little gentle drive as soon as the thermostat opens 13min after your coolant temperature gauge needle is set in the middle your coolant level will drop again quite suddenly you may get a low coolant warning dont worry just pull over leave the engine running and open your hood slowly unscrew the cap while your engine is running and top up with distilled water be careful when unscrewing the cap your coolant system is under high pressure 12 drive for 510 more minutes 13 open your hood and let the coolant in the radiator cool down for 3045min you can check the temperature by touching the upper radiator hose if it has reached approx 40 degrees celsius 104 degrees fahrenheit you can continue you will notice that the coolant level has once again gone down a bit thats normal 14 repeat steps 212 approximately 45 times this ensures that your system is flushed well and that almost all old coolant is flushed out 15 after draining the
